Q: Why does String.intern() change the result of == comparison in Java? A:

== compares object references, not string contents.

String a = "OpsMx";

String b = new String("OpsMx");

  • "OpsMx" (string literal) is placed in the String pool

  • new String("OpsMx") creates a new heap object

So:

a == b   // false

because they are different objects.

Now when you call intern():

String c = b.intern();

intern() checks the String pool:

  • If an identical string already exists, it returns the pooled (canonical) reference

  • Otherwise, it adds the string to the pool and returns it

Since "OpsMx" already exists in the pool:

a == c   // true

Both a and c now point to the same pooled String instance.

Key takeaway

  • == → compares references

  • .equals() → compares values

  • intern() → normalizes strings to a single canonical instance, which can change the result of ==

Best practice

Never rely on == for string comparison.

Use .equals() unless you explicitly need reference identity and fully understand the memory implications of interning.

That’s why String.intern() can change the result of ==, even though the string content itself never changes.

Q: Oracle MERGE causes DuplicateKeyException under high concurrency with composite primary key A:

You have multiple application instances which will be connecting to the database and each will have their own database session. When you have multiple (nearly) simultaneous requests and the primary key does not exist in the database then:

Time Session 1 Session 2
0 start new transaction, MERGE PK
1 start new transaction, MERGE PK
2 Check if PK exists, it does not so perform INSERT
3 Check if PK exists, it does not so perform INSERT
4 COMMIT, succeeds
5 COMMIT, fails with duplicate primary key

At step 3, session 2 checks if the primary key exists but because session 1 has not yet COMMITted their data then session 2 cannot see the new primary key and will try to INSERT (since there is nothing yet to UPDATE) and then when both sessions try to COMMIT then the one that COMMITs first will succeed and the one the COMMITs second will fail with a duplicate primary key exception.

As a thought experiment, consider what the behaviour should be if steps 4 and 5 are reversed and session 2 COMMITs before session 1? In that case, you want session 2 to perform an INSERT and session 1 is going to raise the exception. So, you want both sessions to try to perform the INSERT since neither knows who is going to COMMIT first.

how should this be handled correctly [...]?

Using a MERGE statement does not entirely prevent concurrent requests from having race conditions.

Catch the duplicate primary key exception and send the failed MERGE request a second time (or just send an UPDATE request, since you know that primary key exists).

Q: azure signaturehash rejects my Base64 encoded SHA1 hash from debug.keystore A:

On Android Studio go to View->Tool Windows->Gradle.

On the Gradle tab go to YOURPROJECTNAME->Tasks->android->signingReport.

Right-click on signingReport and left-click on 'Run YOURPROJECTNAME [signingReport]'.

Get the SHA1 from the Run tab generated output on the IDE bottom in the form of xx:xx:xx...xx:xx.

Remove all : from the string above to get pure HEX string

Convert to base 64 here: https://devencode.io/base64-hex (Switch Mode to get Hex -> Base64 Converter)

This base64 string can now be used in Entra Id portal

Q: Adding a new entry to the PATH variable in ZSH A:

Actually, using ZSH allows you to use special mapping of environment variables. So you can simply do (noting that path is lowercase to indicate the array, not the variable):

# append
path+=('/home/david/pear/bin')
# or prepend
path=('/home/david/pear/bin' $path)

# and don't forget to export to make it inherited by child processes
export PATH

For me that's a very neat feature which can be propagated to other variables. Example:

typeset -T LD_LIBRARY_PATH ld_library_path

This is what man zshbuiltins reports about -T.

-T [ scalar[=value] array[=(value ...)] [ sep ] ]
    This flag has a different meaning when used with -f; see below.  Otherwise
    the -T option requires zero, two,  or  three  argu ments  to  be  present.
    With no arguments, the list of parameters created in this fashion is shown.
    With two or three arguments, the first two are the name of a scalar and of
    an array parameter (in that order) that will be tied together in the manner
    of $PATH and $path. The optional third argument is a single-character
    separator which will be used to join  the  elements of the array to form
    the scalar; if absent, a colon is used, as with $PATH. Only the first
    character of the separator is significant;
    any remaining characters are ignored.
    Multibyte characters are not yet supported.

Q: How to disable a Grid and still enable vertical scrolling? A:

IsEnabled is an inherited property, so when you disable the Grid, all of its children are disabled as well, including the ScrollViewer, which is why the vertical scrollbar stops working. A ScrollViewer cannot remain enabled inside a disabled parent. To keep scrolling enabled, the parent container should stay enabled and only the interactive elements should be disabled instead. This can be done by disabling the ListView items (for example via ItemContainerStyle) or by setting IsHitTestVisible on the ListView based on IsConnected, which prevents item selection while still allowing vertical scrolling.

Q: Keyboard shortcut to delete character under/after cursor in vscode? A:

To delete letter Infront of the cursor you can use just Delete button or to delete words Infront of cursor you need to use Ctrl + Delete .

If the cursor is in the insert mode, the delete key does nothing. Change the cursor mode to replace, and the delete key will delete the character to the left of the cursor.
